Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency and cost profile. We're planning a cross-clinic pilot (6 clinics, expected burst periods during mornings) and wanted to ask whether Redwood can provide a one-time ElasticSeat credit to offset the provisioning cost for the first 2 months.

High level:
- Pilot dates: Jan 4 — Mar 4, 2027
- Expected seats (concurrent avg): 35; peak concurrent: ~90 for 2-3 hours/day
- Topline ask: one-time credit equal to 50% of the provisioning delta (~$26k) to make the business case internally

I've attached a short commercial summary and the pilot usage spreadsheet for your model. If helpful, Tom can jump on a call to walk through assumptions.

Would really appreciate if you can route this for an expedited review — procurement cycles are tight.

Thanks,
Sara

Hi Sara — thanks for the details and the attachments. Wrote down a few follow-ups so we can size the ask internally:

- Can you confirm estimated tokens per seat/day during peak hours? (we need sequence-length distribution to model cost)
- Is there a minimum committed spend Elastic Health can take after the pilot? If not, would they accept a smaller credit with a nominal 6-month usage commitment?
- Are there any regulatory/data-retention constraints requiring private deployment or node reservation?

I'll loop in our commercial lead (Marissa) and pricing (Karthik) to get a recommendation. We may treat this as a one-off onboarding credit tied to a short-term commitment to protect unit economics.

Happy to take a quick call with you + Tom to sync — propose Wed 11/04 10:00 PT if that works.

Best,

Kim / Karthik — forwarding Elastic Health request and my read. Quick summary and recommendation below; want this on Marcus's desk for VP/CFO signoff.

Why grant?
- Strategic vertical: health-tech proof point with good reference value and anticipated ARR expansion if pilot succeeds
- Pilot lifts: 6 clinics -> potential to expand to 80 clinics in 12 months if metrics track
- Customer asks for ~50% of provisioning delta (one-time) to cover peak bursting while they validate workflows

Commercial impact (approx):
- Pilot incremental spend (gross) ~ $52k over 2 months; requested credit ~$26k one-time
- We model 18-month expected ARR = $420k if expanded; payback quick if conversion occurs
- Risk: churn after pilot; mitigations: tie credit to 6-month nominal usage minimum OR staged credit (50% upfront, 50% on convert)

Recommendation (preferred):
- Approve a capped one-time ElasticSeat credit of $20k (not to exceed $26k request)
- Condition: 6-month minimal usage commitment at a reduced seat floor OR staged credit (10k upfront, 10k on conversion to paid contract with min commits)
- Add clause: credit reclaim / clawback if onboarding is cancelled within 30 days after pilot end

Supporting artifacts: pricing model and commercial summary attached. Please and confirm if we should route to Marcus for CFO signoff (this exceeds standard SDR credit threshold).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Agree with Marissa's framing. Two quick points to tighten the exception:

1) Make the credit conditional on a minimum committed seat-hours (we should define seat-hours floor per clinic) — this prevents the customer from gaming bursts.
2) Cap exposure: $20k total as recommended; if they want the full $26k we require a 12-month step-down commitment or higher minimum GAU.

If we do staged credit, legal should prepare a short amendment with clawback language. Once Kimberly confirms the floor numbers, I'd be comfortable routing to Marcus for final signoff.

—Karthik
